newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA WARNED ON DRIVE TO SMALL-SCALE MINING.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA WARNED ON DRIVE TO SMALL-SCALE MINING.

text.p: Government's efforts to promote small-scale mining were laudable but had to be approached with caution, Minerals and Energy Policy Centre analyst Mike Solomon said on Wednesday.
Addressing the parliamentary minerals and energy committee, Solomon said small-scale mining had only become an issue over the last few years and very little was in fact known about it.

"The attention that has been focused on the small-scale mining industry is huge and it has a very vocal lobby. They are very well organised and they are making inroads in their cause at very senior levels in government," Solomon said.
But it was impossible for the department of minerals and energy to allocate funds to this sector until more was known about it.
In addition, although mining was a national competency under the new constitution, several provinces were embarking on projects to promote small-scale mining.

As a result, the department needed to make provision for a concerted study into small-scale mining to determine its size, what it was doing and whether it needed institutional support from the government.

"We have no idea whether small-scale mining has a bark bigger than its bite at this stage...And where we as a country are allocating taxpayers' money to developmental issues, we have to be very sure that the sector warrants spending on institutional support," he said.
Experience in several neighbouring countries had proved that if small-scale mining got out of hand it could be "extremely damaging".

"There is very little environmental control and it is very difficult to regulate the industry. However, we have a small- scale mining industry and it needs to be managed and somebody needs to manage it," Solomon said.
"We do not want to spend precious national resources on developing an industry that is going to turn round and bite us and cause major health and safety and environmental problems for the country."
